title: DeepMind maps every 10-meter patch of forest by type, not just tree cover
friendlyTitle: A new map says what kind of forest is there, not just that trees are there
summary: Google DeepMind, Google Research, the World Resources Institute, and IIASA have released Forest Typology 2020, a global map that labels every 10-by-10-meter patch as primary forest, naturally regenerating forest, planted forest, plantation, tree crop, or other land. On more than 9,000 expert-checked sites, it picked the right type 90 percent of the time and separated forest from non-forest 95 percent of the time. An early time series covers 2017 to 2025. The data is on Google Earth Engine under an open license.
friendlySummary: Google DeepMind, Google Research, the World Resources Institute, and IIASA have released a global map called Forest Typology 2020. It labels every 10-by-10-meter patch as primary forest, forest that grew back, planted forest, a timber plantation, a tree crop, or other land. On more than 9,000 sites checked by experts, it picked the right type 90 percent of the time. It told forest from non-forest 95 percent of the time. An early year-by-year series covers 2017 to 2025. The data is free on Google Earth Engine.
whyItMatters: A green pixel is not a natural forest. If you buy coffee, cocoa, palm oil, or wood, or you have to show that a product did not come from cleared primary forest, the useful map is the one that says what replaced the trees. The time series is an early release. The probability scores let you set a stricter cutoff instead of trusting a single yes-or-no label.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Green on a satellite photo is not the same as an old natural forest. If you buy coffee, cocoa, palm oil, or wood, or you have to show a product did not come from cleared primary forest, you need a map that says what replaced the trees. This time series is an early release. The confidence scores let you set a stricter cutoff instead of trusting one yes-or-no label.
